Xhandy

Brand guidelines · v8 · 2026-10-20 · generated from brand.yaml

Identity

Xhandy puts post heat, your relationship with the author and your interaction history next to every post, so you can see which ones are worth a reply.

Short
Quiet hints while you use X
Long
Xhandy is a browser extension for people who engage on X by hand. Next to every post it shows how old the post is and how fast it is getting views, whether you and the author follow each other, and how often you have interacted. It warns you before you send a near-duplicate reply. It never clicks or sends anything for you, keeps all data in your browser, and is free and open source.
Positioning
For people who grow on X by replying and engaging by hand: Xhandy shows post heat, your relationship with the author and your interaction history right next to every post, so you can see which ones are worth a reply. Other extensions each cover one of these; Xhandy covers them all, and never acts for you.

Audience

Simplified-Chinese creators with X Premium who grow by engaging by hand and care about views and payouts (primary audience)
They can't tell which posts are worth replying to, and checking who follows them back or how often they've talked means opening profiles or hovering over avatars

English-speaking X users who engage by hand (secondary audience)
The same: no quick way to see which posts deserve a reply, and follow status and past interactions are hidden behind clicks

Not for

  • People who want growth on autopilot: auto-follow, auto-reply, engagement bots

Refuses to be

  • A tool that acts for you: it never clicks, types, sends, likes, follows or unfollows, and does nothing in bulk
  • A data collector: no network requests, no analytics, no remote code; your data stays in your browser
  • A speed tool that makes accounts look like bots: soft daily limits on follows and unfollows, and warnings on repeated replies

Personality

PlainLabels you read at a glance, like "2h · 15K/h"not a flashy analytics dashboard
SavvyKnows how X works: posts over 48 hours old go grey, repeated replies look like spamnot preachy
HandyStays out of the way: keyboard shortcuts, overlays that never block a clicknot feature bloat

No network, your data stays in your browserOnly two permissions, storage and unlimitedStorage; no network requests, analytics or remote code; export, import or delete everything
See which posts are taking offOrange from 1,000 views an hour, red with 🔥 from 10,000; posts older than 48 hours go grey
Remembers where you stand with every authorShows follow status (⇄ mutual / → you follow / ← follows you / not following), how often you have interacted and when you last did
All of it in one extensionPost age and heat, follow status, interaction history, duplicate-reply warnings, daily stats, the follow assistant and the "not following you back" panel
Free and open sourcePublic repository jackxlabs/xhandy; download from GitHub Releases
Chinese and English interfaceChinese when the browser language is Chinese, English otherwise

Voice

Xhandy talks like a friend sitting next to you: says little, and every line is useful

formal / casual
Clear like good docs; neither stiff nor jokey
serious / playful
Mostly serious, with the occasional light line
plain / technical
Plain words; technical terms swapped for what users would say
reserved / bold
Understated; no inflated claims, limits stated openly

Traits

Plain

Do: Lead with the result and a real number
Don't: Stacked adjectives, vague "boost" or "optimise"

Xhandy's smart engine analyses post performance to supercharge your growth!

Posts getting over 10,000 views an hour turn red, so you can see what's taking off.

Savvy

Do: Give the X-specific reason in half a sentence
Don't: Lecturing, or long lists of warnings

For your account's safety, please be careful not to follow too many people too frequently.

Xhandy reminds you after 20 follows a day: following fast can get an account limited.

Handy

Do: Say which key to press and where to look
Don't: Long feature tours

Take advantage of our thoughtfully designed keyboard shortcuts to dramatically boost your productivity.

Select a post and press Shift+F: focus jumps to the author's Follow button.

Use / not

UseNotWhy
posttweetX's own term since 2023; the README and UI use post
XTwitterThe platform's current name
mutual, follows you backfollow-back, F4FUI wording; F4F reads as follow-for-follow schemes

Never say

growth hack, game-changer, supercharge, 10x, unlockEmpty hype that clashes with being plain

Style

  • numbers: Real numbers and thresholds (1,000/h, 20 a day, 48 hours), never "tons" or "lots"; thousands separators in prose, 15K style in labels
  • spacing_and_case: Sentence case for headings, buttons and titles; product and feature names as written in the UI
  • punctuation: No exclamation marks; UI names in quotes or bold, not both; Oxford comma optional, keep each document consistent
  • emoji: No emoji in product copy; the UI only uses 🔥 for hot posts and ⇄ → ← for follow status
  • emphasis: Bold only for warnings and key steps, e.g. "keep the folder where it is"
  • person: Address the reader as "you"; Xhandy refers to itself by name, not "we"; contractions are fine
  • limits: State limits plainly, e.g. "this list is partial", "X may have changed its data, so don't trust this list"
  • spelling: US or UK spelling, one per document (the README leans UK: 'colours', 'greyed out'; keep UK unless Jack prefers US); keyboard keys as Shift+F, Alt+U

Channels

readmeformat: Docs style: one line on what it is, then features with screenshots; Chinese and English sections; tone: Clear and specific
release_notesformat: Use docs/release-template.md; one or two sentences on changes users will notice; tone: Matter-of-fact
store_listingformat: Short one-liner first, then the features, ending with the X Corp non-affiliation line; length: Title up to 45 characters; short description up to 132
uiformat: One line, numbers first; on errors say the likely cause and the next step, never blame the user; tone: Remind, don't command
x_postformat: When Jack mentions Xhandy on his own account, it is his experience in his voice (jack-personal-brand x-voice-guide); tone: Jack's voice
